full_judgment:
Nurul Huque Bhuiyan, J.:—This Rule under section 561A read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka and the Opposite Party No.1 to show cause why the proceeding in Petition Case No.461a1 of 1987 pending in the court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should not be quashed. 

 3. The petitioner appeared before the Chief Metropolitan. Magistrate, Dhaka on 17.6.87 and he was admitted to bail. On 21.7.87 the complainant submitted an application before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka praying for directing the petitioner to produce the minor child and also for cancellation of the bail of the petitioner. In the meantime suppressing the above fact the complainant moved an application for cancellation of bail of the petitioner on 3.8.87 before the Sessions Judge, Dhaka and it was numbered as Crl. Misc. Case No.1441/87. The learned Sessions Judge on hearing both the parties held the view that the application was premature and there was little scope for the Criminal Court to determine the custody of the minor child in favour of the mother, that it could only be done under the Guardian and Wards Act and that there was no allegation against the father (Petitioner) as to the welfare of the child. Accordingly he rejected the application by his order dated 30.6.87. After the disposal of the above Criminal Misc. Case No. 1441/87 the complainant moved a fresh application before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka for production of her minor son in court on lO.9.87. The learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka by order dated 20.10.87 directed the petitioner to produce the minor son in court on 8.11.87. On 8.11.87 the petitioner moved the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate to review the order dated 20.10.87 but by an order of even date the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate rejected the plaintiffs prayer. Against the orders dated 

 20.1 0.87 and 8.11.87 the petitioner moved the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka in Crl. Revision No.385 of 1987 which was transferred to the Addl. Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka for disposal and the learned Additional Sessions Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka by order dated 11.4.88 rejected the application, on humanitarian ground. In his absence on 26.11.87 the learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka cancelled the bail and issued warrant of arrest against the petitioner and as soon as the petitioner came to know about this order he surrendered before the learned Sessions Judge, Dhaka who granted him bail and confirmed the same by his order 8.2.88 in Cr!. Misc. Case No. 266/88. 

 5. Mr. Zinnur Ahmd, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the father petitioner being the legal guardian of the minor child has in Law the constructive custody of the child and can claim that he bonafide believed himself entitled to the custody of the child and thus not guilty of kidnapping his own child when he removed him from the custody of the mother. In support of his submission, he relies upon the decisions in the cases of Imambandi Vs. Mutsaddi, I.L.R. 45 Cal(P.C.)878; Ahmed Nawazl and others Vs. The State, 20 DLR (W.P),45 ; Bashir Ahmed Vs. The State, 22 D.L.R. (W.P.) 312 and Ismail Aboobaker, Puthuparambil, ThoduPuzka and others Vs. State of Kerala, A.I.R. 1968. Ker. 

 6. In the case reported in ILR.4S Cal (P.C.)878 the Privy Council held' "By Mahomedan Law the mother is entitled only to the custody of the person of her minor child up to a certain age according to the sex of the child. B\R she is not the natural guardian the father alone or if he be dead his executor (under the Sunni Law) is the legal guardian". 

 In the case reported in 20 DLR (W.P.) 45 following the Privy Council decision in ILR 45 Cal (P.C.)878 it was held: "Under the Muhammadan Law the father is the legal guardian of the minor children. The legal guardian has in law constructive custody of the minor children. He can also claim that he bonafide believed himself entitled to their custody and thus not guilty of kidnaping his own children when be removes them from the hizanat (custody) of the mother". 

 In the case reported in 22 DLR(W.P.) 324 it was held following the Privy Council decision in !LR..45 Cal (P.C.)878. 

 In the case reported in AIR 1968 Kerala 21 it was held: 'Under the Sunni School of Mohammedan Law the mother is entitled to the custody of male child until the child reaches the age of 7 years. The father is the natural and legal guardian of minor. A legal guardian is certainly a lawful guardian, and if he takes minor child of 2-1(2 years from the custody of the mother who is not the legal or natural guardian though entitled to the custody of child until it reaches a particular age he can not be said to commit the offence of kidnapping as he does not take the child out of the keeping of the lawful guardian. The right of the mother to the custody of the minor child is something different from the right of the lawful guardian. The right is subject to the superior right of lawful guardian". 

 In the instant case the proceedings were drawn up by the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka against the petitioner u/s. 363 of the Penal Code which runs as follows :- 

 8. Against the decisions cited by the learned Advocate for the petitioner Mrs. Fowzia Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1, has referred to the case of the State Vs. Ramji Vithal Chaudhuri and another, A.I.R. 1958 Born. 381. In this case in a suit for divorce by the Hindu wife, the Court after decreeing the Suit directed that their minor girl was to remain in the custody of the mother till the father (husband) got himself appointed as the guardian of the minor under the Guesclin’s and Wards Act. The order was made by virtue of section 15 of the Bombay Hindu Divorce Act, 1947 and the mother was the lawful guardian of the minor by virtue of that order. If the father who was living separately forcibly took away the minor girl from the keeping of the lawful guardian without the consent of such lawful guardian action of the father amounted to kidnapping. In this case the Court after decreeing the suit for divorce directed that the minor girl was to remain in the custody of the mother till the father got himself appointed as the guardian of the minor under the Guardian and Wards Act. 

 9. In the said case there was a direction from court under section 15 of the Hindu Divorce Act, 1947 that till the father was appointed as the guardian of the minor child the child would remain in the custody of the mother and that was in the interest and welfare of the child but in the instant case there is no such direction from court. Thus on facts the case reported in AIR 1958 Born. 381 is distinguishable from the present case and as such the principle laid down in the said case will not be applicable in the present case. 

 11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the proceedings in the Petition Case No.461a1 of 1987 pending in the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka, are quashed.
